canonical_base_note: the admitted venue is the Debian official image, pinned by digest (the `debian` Docker Hub base the court Dockerfile builds FROM), and it is the smallest practical admitted base for this stratum. The running court image `openssl-rs-court:1` is the environment every entry point records in PHASE25_IMAGE; the base is the one source the tool-specific environments are derived from rather than a second, drifting base.
derivation_policy: Phase 25 runs one tool-specific environment per instrument -- the compiler-backed census, Miri, ASan, MSan, TSan, Kani and the CVE replays -- and every one of them is derived from the single minimal base this manifest names, in later subphases. The stratum deliberately does not maintain one mutable kitchen-sink image that accumulates every tool: a kitchen-sink image makes the environment a function of whoever last rebuilt it, so a result depends on state nothing binds, whereas deriving each environment from one pinned base makes the toolchain a fact the manifest records. The running court image `openssl-rs-court:1` is the admitted venue the guard binds; a later subphase that needs an extra tool adds a derived environment and records it here rather than widening the court image.
selection_rule: Phase 25 executes only inside the admitted court container. This committed manifest records the one admitted venue -- the container marker, the opt-in environment flag, and the image identity and platform the venue records in the environment -- and `forensics/tools/phase25_guard.py` fails closed unless every one of them is present and matches. Nothing about the memory-safety census, the sanitizers, the proof harnesses or the CVE replays is built, run or probed outside this venue (docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md section 1). The canonical base is the minimal Debian image the venue is built from; the tool-specific environments are derived from it in later subphases rather than being separate admitted bases.
metadata_only_rule: `metadata_only` names the Phase-25 generators that read committed atlases and write a derived plane -- they execute nothing, no compiler, no tool, no probe -- so the guard admits them on any host exactly as the other strata's obligation generators run host-side in CI's static job. `phase25_obligations.py` is the ledger, `ms_obligations.py` (25.3) is a pure derivation over the committed 25.1 census and 25.2 non-Rust TCB, `ms_ownership_planes.py` (25.4) is a pure derivation over the committed census, the committed TCB and the committed source text, `ms_phase22_crosswalk.py` (25.5) is a pure derivation over the committed census and the committed Phase-22 atlas, `ms_phase24_crosswalk.py` (25.6) is a pure derivation over the committed census, the committed 25.5 crosswalk and the committed Phase-24 downstream measurement, and `ms_exposure.py` (25.7) is a pure derivation over the committed census, the committed 25.5 crosswalk, the committed 25.6 crosswalk and the committed 25.4 ownership planes: none runs a compiler and none builds anything, so each is admitted beside the ledger. Every execution entry point (the runner `phase25_courts.py`, and every later subphase tool that compiles the census, runs Miri/ASan/MSan/TSan/Kani or replays a CVE) is deliberately absent from this list, so a host invocation of one is refused. A pure derivation that reads only committed Phase-25 artefacts (and the committed source it classifies, the committed Phase-22 atlas it reads, or the committed Phase-24 measurement it joins to) and writes a derived plane is admitted beside `phase25_obligations.py` in the commit that lands it, exactly as the Phase-24 derivations are, and any tool that compiles, instruments, proves or replays stays deliberately absent and is refused on the host.
non_claims: the admitted venue is a container identity, not a security boundary: it records where Phase 25 runs, not what it may claim

the manifest is authored evidence, not proof the container is unmodified: it binds the venue a receipt names, and the base digest is the stronger binding a later subphase may carry into each derived environment
admitting a metadata-only generator on the host is not admitting host execution: that generator runs no command and produces no runtime evidence
naming one canonical base is not claiming the base is byte-identical to every derived environment: each derived environment is recorded as its own derivation when a later subphase lands it
